alcachofas-guisadas-de-la-abuela.title: Grandma's Braised Artichokes
alcachofas-guisadas-de-la-abuela.subtitle: The humble stew that fills the kitchen with the smell of home
alcachofas-guisadas-de-la-abuela.description: Fresh artichokes braised slowly with garlic, smoked pimentón de la Vera and a little jamón until tender and silky. Grandma's recipe, exactly as it was made on any ordinary Thursday.
alcachofas-guisadas-de-la-abuela.note: Grandma served them with the thickened broth, for mopping with bread. Leftovers are even better the next day.

steps.name: Trim
steps.text: Remove the tough outer leaves of the artichokes down to the pale heart. Peel and trim the stem, cut off the top. Quarter them and drop into lemon water so they don't darken.

steps.name: Sauté
steps.text: In a clay pot, heat the oil and sauté the sliced garlic over medium heat until barely golden. Add the jamón and give it a few turns.

steps.name: Pimentón and flour
steps.text: Pull the pot off the heat for a moment, add the pimentón and flour and stir fast — pimentón turns bitter if it burns.

steps.name: Braise
steps.text: Add the drained artichokes, the bay leaf and enough broth to nearly cover. Cover and cook gently for 35–40 minutes, until tender.

steps.name: Rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let it sit 10 minutes lid on. The broth thickens and the artichokes settle into their flavor.

paella-valenciana.title: Paella Valenciana
paella-valenciana.subtitle: Sunday's rice, with the rules made clear
paella-valenciana.description: The real paella: chicken, rabbit, garrofón beans and flat green beans, bomba rice and saffron. No chorizo, no rushing, and the socarrat crust as the final reward.
paella-valenciana.note: The classic ratio is three parts broth to one of rice, but bomba drinks a little more. Better to come up short on broth and get socarrat than to overcook it soft.

steps.name: Brown the meat
steps.text: Heat the oil in the paella pan and brown the salted chicken and rabbit over high heat, unhurried, until well crusted on all sides. This step decides the rice's flavor.

steps.name: Vegetables
steps.text: Add the green beans and garrofón and fry a few minutes. Push everything aside, put the grated tomato in the center and fry until it darkens.

steps.name: Pimentón and broth
steps.text: Add the pimentón, stir, and pour in the water. Add the saffron and boil 15 minutes so the meat finishes cooking and the broth takes flavor.

steps.name: Rice
steps.text: Spread the rice in a cross shape and level it — from here on, no stirring. Taste the broth and adjust salt.

steps.name: Cook
steps.text: 8 minutes over high heat, 10 over low. In the last 2 minutes lay the rosemary sprig on top.

steps.name: Socarrat
steps.text: Crank the heat to maximum for the final 30–60 seconds, until you hear a soft crackle: that's the socarrat forming. Rest 5 minutes covered with a cloth.

tortilla-de-patatas.title: Spanish Potato Tortilla
tortilla-de-patatas.subtitle: Thick, runny in the middle, golden outside
tortilla-de-patatas.description: The classic Spanish tortilla: potatoes confited slowly in olive oil, egg, and the confident flip. With onion, as this house rules.
tortilla-de-patatas.note: Better eggs, better tortilla. And resting the mixture before cooking is the trick almost nobody mentions.

steps.name: Cut
steps.text: Slice the potatoes thin (or small dice, as your household prefers) and julienne the onion.

steps.name: Confit
steps.text: Put the potatoes and onion in a pan with the cold oil and salt. Cook over medium-low heat 20–25 minutes, without browning: they should soften like a confit.

steps.name: Mix
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and onion (save the oil for another day) and fold them into the beaten, salted eggs in a large bowl. Rest 10 minutes — the potato drinks the egg.

steps.name: Set
steps.text: Pour into a nonstick pan with two spoonfuls of the oil. Over medium-high heat, set the edges 2–3 minutes, pressing a flat plate on top to compact it.

steps.name: The flip
steps.text: Using the plate, turn it over with conviction and slide the tortilla back into the pan. Cook 2 more minutes: the center should stay runny.

gazpacho-andaluz.title: Andalusian Gazpacho
gazpacho-andaluz.subtitle: Liquid summer, of ripe tomato and yesterday's bread
gazpacho-andaluz.description: Tomato, cucumber, pepper, bread, olive oil and vinegar: the authentic Andalusian gazpacho, blended smooth and served properly cold. Not a fashionable soup — a way to survive August.
gazpacho-andaluz.note: Without truly ripe tomatoes there is no gazpacho worth the name. In winter, don't even try.

steps.name: Soak
steps.text: Soak the bread crumb in a little water while you prep the vegetables.

steps.name: Blend
steps.text: Put everything in the blender — chopped tomatoes, peeled cucumber, pepper, drained bread, garlic, salt and vinegar — and blend for longer than you think: at least 2–3 minutes, until not a strand remains.

steps.name: Emulsify
steps.text: With the blender running, add the olive oil in a thin stream at the end. That's what gives body and shine.

steps.name: Strain and chill
steps.text: Pass through a fine sieve, pressing with a spoon, and refrigerate at least 2 hours. Serve very cold with croutons and diced vegetables.

fabada-asturiana.title: Asturian Fabada
fabada-asturiana.subtitle: The bean stew with compango, for days of serious eating
fabada-asturiana.description: Asturian fabes simmered slowly with compango — chorizo, morcilla blood sausage and lacón — until the beans are meltingly tender and the broth thickens on its own.
fabada-asturiana.note: Fabada is never stirred with a spoon: the pot is shaken. And genuine Asturian fabes if you can find them — there is no honest substitute.

steps.name: Soak
steps.text: Soak the fabes overnight, 12 hours, in cold water.

steps.name: Start
steps.text: Put the drained fabes in a wide pot with the whole compango, onion, garlic, bay leaf and cold water to cover by two fingers. Bring to a boil.

steps.name: Skim
steps.text: Skim the foam off the surface and lower the heat to minimum.

steps.name: Slow cook
steps.text: Simmer 2 to 2½ hours on the lowest heat, shaking the pot back and forth now and then (never a spoon — the fabes break). Add cold water in small splashes if they run dry: the shock helps them turn tender.

steps.name: Rest
steps.text: Take out the compango, slice it and return it. Let the fabada rest at least 30 minutes before serving. Next day, spectacular.

salmorejo-cordobes.title: Cordoban Salmorejo
salmorejo-cordobes.subtitle: Thick, emulsified, topped with jamón and egg
salmorejo-cordobes.description: Gazpacho's Cordoban cousin: more bread, much thicker, no cucumber or pepper, crowned with serrano ham and hard-boiled egg. A textbook tomato cream.
salmorejo-cordobes.note: Real salmorejo holds a spoon upright. If it pours, it needs more bread or more blending.

steps.name: Base
steps.text: Blend the chopped tomatoes until fine. Add the bread in pieces and let it soak 10 minutes.

steps.name: Blend
steps.text: Blend bread and tomato with the salt and vinegar into a dense, homogeneous cream.

steps.name: Oil
steps.text: Add the olive oil in a thin stream with the blender running, until it emulsifies and the cream lightens a shade.

steps.name: Serve
steps.text: Cold, with chopped jamón and grated egg on top. In Córdoba it's drunk from a glass.

pisto-manchego.title: Pisto Manchego
pisto-manchego.subtitle: La Mancha's ratatouille, with a fried egg on top
pisto-manchego.description: Tomato, pepper, zucchini and onion, diced and cooked slowly. The honest Manchego pisto, served with a fried egg or bread crumbs.
pisto-manchego.note: Pisto is slow pan work: each vegetable joins when its turn comes, not all at once.

steps.name: Dice
steps.text: Cut the onion, pepper and zucchini into small, even dice. The Manchego way, always — no giant chunks.

steps.name: In order
steps.text: Poach the onion in the oil 8 minutes, add the pepper for 10 more, then the zucchini for another 10.

steps.name: Tomato
steps.text: Add the grated tomato and a pinch of sugar. Cook over medium heat 25–30 minutes, uncovered, until the water evaporates and the pisto has body.

steps.name: Serve
steps.text: With a fried egg on top and bread. Also cold the next day, or as a base for baked eggs.

caldo-gallego.title: Galician Broth (Caldo Gallego)
caldo-gallego.subtitle: The bone-and-grelos broth that restores you
caldo-gallego.description: The honest Galician caldo: lard, ham bone, white beans, turnip greens and potato. A winter dish eaten by the spoonful beside the hearth.
caldo-gallego.note: Breaking the potato instead of cutting it isn't a quirk: the rough surface releases starch and thickens the broth.

steps.name: Cook the base
steps.text: Put the soaked beans with the bone, lard and chorizo in plenty of cold water. Bring to a boil, then down to minimum.

steps.name: Ninety minutes
steps.text: Simmer 90 minutes on low, skimming at the start. Add cold water in small doses if needed — again, the shock softens the legume.

steps.name: Potato and greens
steps.text: Add the broken-up potatoes in big pieces and the chopped grelos. Cook 25 minutes more, until the potato releases and the broth thickens.

steps.name: Serve
steps.text: Remove the lard and bone, slice the chorizo back in and serve piping hot, with cornbread if you have it.

escalivada-catalana.title: Catalan Escalivada
escalivada-catalana.subtitle: Vegetables roasted over direct heat, dressed with nothing else
escalivada-catalana.description: Peppers, eggplant, onion and tomato roasted over a flame or in the oven, peeled into strips and dressed only with olive oil and salt. Escalivada is the Catalan summer on a plate.
escalivada-catalana.note: The tap is escalivada's enemy: rinsing the strips throws away half the roast.

steps.name: Roast
steps.text: Roast the whole vegetables in a 220 °C oven (or over an open flame, the old way): peppers and eggplant 35–40 minutes, onions and tomatoes for the last 20.

steps.name: Sweat
steps.text: Move them to a bowl and cover, or wrap in paper, 15 minutes: the steam loosens the skins.

steps.name: Peel and strip
steps.text: Peel with your hands — never under the tap, it washes away the flavor — and cut lengthwise into strips, over a plate to catch the juices.

steps.name: Dress
steps.text: Arrange the strips on a platter, salt and dress with their own juices and olive oil. Rest at least half an hour. Serve warm or cold, with anchovies or without.

crema-catalana.title: Crema Catalana
crema-catalana.subtitle: The burnt custard done with the iron, since Sant Josep
crema-catalana.description: Milk cream with cinnamon and lemon, thickened with cornstarch and covered with sugar burnt to order with the iron or a blowtorch. The fiesta mayor dessert.
crema-catalana.note: Cornstarch and yolks, not flour or gelatin: crema catalana cuts clean, it doesn't bounce.

steps.name: Infuse
steps.text: Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick and lemon peel to a boil. Turn off, cover and steep 10 minutes.

steps.name: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch until pale. Strain the milk into the mixture, slowly, stirring.

steps.name: Cook
steps.text: Return everything to medium heat and stir constantly with a spatula or whisk until it thickens — 5–7 minutes from the first steam. Do not boil.

steps.name: Portion
steps.text: Pour into small clay dishes and smooth the surface. Chill at least 3 hours.

steps.name: Burn
steps.text: Cover each cream with a thin layer of sugar and burn with a hot iron or blowtorch to an amber crust. Serve at once — the contrast is the dish.
